content.text:
The user wants me to create a game like GTA San Andreas in Unity. This is an enormously ambitious request — GTA San Andreas is a massive open-world game that took Rockstar years and hundreds of developers to build. I obviously can't recreate that, but I can create a Unity project skeleton with core GTA-style mechanics: third-person character controller, vehicle driving, a city, wanted system, pedestrians, camera system, etc.

I can't actually run Unity here (no Unity editor in this environment), but I can write a complete, well-structured Unity project — scripts, scene setup instructions, prefab descriptions, etc. — that the user can open in Unity.

Should I ask a clarifying question first? The environment is a Playground repo. Let me check what's in the working directory first. Actually, the request is clear enough — build a Unity project. The reasonable deliverable: a Unity project structure with C# scripts implementing:

1. Third-person player controller (walk/run/jump/sprint)
2. Vehicle entry/exit system (like GTA - press F to enter car)
3. Car driving controller (arcade physics)
4. Third/fourth person camera with mouse look + follow
5. NPC/pedestrian wander AI
6. Police/wanted star system
7. Minimap
8. Simple city generator (procedural blocks of roads/buildings) so no need for assets
9. Shooting (simple raycast)
10. Health system, HUD

All using primitives (capsules, boxes) so it works without external assets. I could also generate the scene via an editor script so the user can build the whole city in one click. That's a great approach: an Editor script that generates the scene — roads, buildings, cars, peds — everything from primitives.

Let me check the working directory first to see if there's an existing repo structure I should be aware of.

Plan:
- Create folder `GTASanAndreasClone/` (Unity project structure: Assets/, ProjectSettings won't be complete but Unity will generate them when opened; actually I should create minimal ProjectSettings so Unity Hub can open it as a project... Creating a full Unity project requires ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt and Packages/manifest.json — Unity can then generate the rest of Library etc.)
- Write scripts: Player, Vehicle, NPC, Police, WantedSystem, GameManager, CameraController, Minimap, HUD, Weapon.

Let me design:

Project name: "SanAndreasClone" under Assets in the checkout? Working dir is a repo "PlayGround". I'll create a folder in the repo like `SanAndreasUnityClone/`.

Files:

```
SanAndreasClone/
  README.md (setup instructions)
  ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt
  Packages/manifest.json
  Assets/
    Scripts/
      Core/GameManager.cs
      Player/PlayerController.cs
      Player/PlayerInteraction.cs (enter/exit vehicles)
      Player/Shooting/WeaponSystem.cs
      Vehicles/VehicleController.cs
      Vehicles/VehicleManager.cs
      NPCs/NPCController.cs
      NPCs/NPCManager.cs
      Police/WantedSystem.cs
      Police/PoliceOfficer.cs
      Camera/CameraController.cs
      UI/HUD.cs
      UI/Minimap.cs
      World/CityGenerator.cs / EditorCityBuilder
    Editor/
      SceneBuilder.cs (BuildScene menu)
  ...
```

Important: CityGenerator as a regular Monobehaviour with "RUNTIME" generation is easy, but an editor "Build Scene" menu is nicer. Actually simplest robust: a `WorldBuilder` MonoBehaviour that you attach to an empty GameObject in an empty scene; in Start() it instantiates everything. But one-click editor scene building is nicer for people who want to inspect. I could support both: make the builder code that works both at runtime and in editor via a static method with #if UNITY_EDITOR guarded? To keep it simpler: do a pure-runtime `WorldBuilder` — press Play and the city appears. That works in any Unity version with zero editor API issues. Plus a small editor script for generating. Hmm, keep it runtime-only to avoid compile issues, and give instructions.

Vehicle enter/exit: player approaches car, press F; player GameObject gets disabled or parented; camera target changes.

Physics: use WheelCollider for the car for realism, but many people struggle to tune WheelColliders. Arcade-style Rigidbody driving (transform-forward force + steering torque) is more reliable and feels GTA-lite. I'll do a Rigidbody-based arcade controller: apply force along forward, steer by rotating velocity direction / applying torque. Simpler and robust.

Camera: orbit third-person camera with mouse; follows player or vehicle with different distances.

Shooting: raycast from camera forward, muzzle at player head; NPCs get hit; wanted level increases.

NPCs: wander waypoints; flee when shots nearby; ragdoll-lite = just fall over (rotate) and die.

Police: spawn cops depending on wanted stars; cops chase on foot (simple); wanted decays if you hide.

HUD: health bar, wanted stars, money, weapon ammo, current vehicle speed.

Money: pickups? Killing peds gives money (GTA-ish). Keep simple: HUD money increments when picking up coins scattered, or killing NPC.

UI: use OnGUI (IMGUI) to avoid needing TextMeshPro assets/setup. OnGUI works everywhere with zero setup. For a demo that's pragmatic. Minimap: render camera top-down into a Texture via RenderTexture and draw with OnGUI — easy.

GameManager singleton to coordinate spawning.

Road network: grid city — roads every X meters, sidewalk, buildings in blocks, some parks, traffic cars driving along roads with simple waypoint logic (straight, turn at intersections randomly). Traffic: keep cars moving along lanes with grid navigation. Simpler: traffic cars move along a straight road, and at intersections pick random direction. I'll implement grid-based waypoints.

Let me carefully write cohesive, compile-safe C# code. Should be careful about API differences; stick to very standard APIs (UnityEngine.CoreModule, PhysicsModule, UIModule for OnGUI). Unity 2021.3+ LTS assumed. Write ProjectVersion.txt with 2022.3.x. manifest.json with core packages only.

Let me define grid: cell size 60 (block: road width 12 + sidewalk 3 each side + building area). Roads run along x and z lines every 60m from -300..300 (11 lines each way?) Let's define cityHalf = 5 blocks => coordinates: road center lines at multiples of 60, from -300 to 300. City area 600x600.

CityGenerator builds:
- Ground plane (grass color) 700x700.
- For each road line: box (asphalt) width 14.
- Intersections automatically overlap fine (same material).
- Lane markings: skip or add thin boxes. Skip for simplicity, maybe dashed lines: could add small white strips. Nice-to-have; add cheap dashes along roads.
- Blocks: within each block (between roads), place 1-4 buildings (boxes with randomHeight 8-40), colored gray variants, plus windows via emissive? Too much. Just colored boxes with slightly random hues. Add door/counters.

Actually building generation: block interior area spanning (60-14)/... define: road occupies ±7 around road center. Block from roadCenter+7 (plus sidewalk 4) to next roadCenter-7-4. Block interior size = 60 - 14 - 8 = 38. Place 1 building 20x20..30x30 footprint, height 8..35; fill leftover with grass/park or smaller buildings.

Colliders: primitives auto have colliders via AddComponent<BoxCollider>.

Vehicle: prefab built from code: body box + cabin box + 4 wheels (cylinders rotated) + Rigidbody + our VehicleController. Wheels visual only (no WheelCollider) — arcade.

WheelSpinVisual: rotate wheel meshes by speed.

Traffic system: waypoints at intersections; each traffic car picks next node, drives using simple steering toward waypoint. When destroyed or stuck, respawn / recycle. Keep ~15 traffic cars.

Peds: capsule with body; wander between random points on sidewalks; die on hit by car (vehicle checks collision with NPC via trigger? collider speed check) — simplest: check in NPC's OnCollisionEnter for vehicle rigidbody velocity>. Every frame distance check between vehicles and NPCs, if < threshold and vehicle speed high, kill. Use overlap sphere from vehicle each interval. That's cheap enough.

Player: capsule with head sphere, Rigidbody kinematic? Use CharacterController component for player movement — standard. Third-person movement: move relative to camera, rotate toward move direction; when aiming (right mouse) face camera forward.

Weapon: pistol & SMG; shoot via raycast, spawn muzzle flash light? Keep: line renderer tracer + shell? Tracer: draw a small stretched box or LineRenderer for 0.05s.

Wanted system: levels 0-6 stars; crimes add "heat"; police spawn near player; cops shoot player (raycast with cooldown, apply damage). Wanted decays after no crime for a while, faster if out of sight (distance check).

Death/respawn: respawn at hospital with money penalty, wanted reset. Classic GTA.

Save logic: GameManager static Instance.

HUD: OnGUI drawing textures (use Texture2D created at runtime white texture and GUI.Box/Label; stars via ★ characters). Money in yellow. Health bar red. Speed when in car. Minimap: RT camera top-down following player; also draw blips? drawing blips on minimap requires world→map math; doable: positions relative to player scaled. I'll draw simple dots for peds/police/cars on the minimap rect. Nice.

That's a lot of code but let's write it well and compactly. Aim for ~1500-2500 lines total across files. Keep each file focused, well-commented.

Also README with setup:
1. Unity Hub install 2022.3 LTS
2. Open project folder
3. Create empty scene, add WorldBuilder? Better: SceneBuilder editor menu "GTA/Build San Andreas Scene" that creates everything including WorldBuilder objects. Let me include an editor script that creates the scene (EditorSceneManager.NewScene, then builds). The WorldBuilder static BuildAllWorld() used both by editor (instantiating into scene, marked undo-able? not needed) and runtime Start.

Simplest architecture: `WorldBuilder` Mono with `public bool buildOnStart` and static `BuildAll(Transform parent)`. Editor menu creates new scene, calls WorldBuilder.BuildAll, saves scene. Runtime Start calls BuildAll too. One code path.

But building in editor: Editor scripts can't reference runtime-assembly Monobehaviour statics? They can — editor assembly references runtime assembly, so calling WorldBuilder.BuildAll from an editor script is fine as long as it's not #if UNITY_EDITOR wrapped in runtime code.

Components wiring: code does everything in EnsureComponent calls; references found via FindObjectOfType at runtime for cross-refs (GameManager). VehicleController referencing VehicleManager via static Instance. Fine.

Materials: create via ScriptableObject? At runtime: new Material(Shader.Find("Standard")). Careful: Shader.Find("Standard") works if Standard shader included (always in Built-in RP; in URP not). Set project as Built-in Render Pipeline in manifest? Built-in is default when no URP package. To be safe, note in README use Built-in 3D template. Since we create ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt only, Unity asks for template? Opening a folder with ProjectVersion sets version but missing template files; Unity handles it: opening incomplete project works (it imports Assets and regenerates ProjectSettings defaults). It generally works: creating manifest.json + ProjectVersion.txt + Assets, Unity opens it fine as built-in.

Shader fallback: try Shader.Find("Standard"), if null use Shader.Find("Universal Render Pipeline/Lit"), if null use Shader.Find("HDRP/Lit")? I'll write a MaterialHelper that tries several and caches; plus fallback to "Legacy Shaders/Diffuse" which is always available! Great: "Legacy Shaders/Diffuse" ships with all pipelines. Use that for guaranteed compile. Colors of legacy diffuse support _Color. Good.

Specular-ish feel: keep diffuse; fine.

OnGUI for all UI - uses legacy GUISkin fonts; fine.

Money pickups: floating green coin (cylinder) rotate & bob; on pickup +$.

Sounds: could synthesize via AudioClip.Create procedurally (engine hum, gunshot). That's fun but adds complexity; maybe add simple procedural gunshot beep? I'll skip audio to keep bugs low, maybe include lightweight sound manager with pure-sine/mean synthesized tones for gunshot, pickup, star. AudioClip.Create with delegate samples — works. I'll add small `Sfx.cs` and call guards. Risk: plays ok. I'll include it - it's contained.

Let me be careful about correctness:

CharacterController: attach, radius .3, height 1.7, center (0, .9? no: center y = height/2 offset). For capsule-based character: position pivot at feet? Standard: GameObject at ground; CharacterController center (0,1,0) height 1.8. I'll set that.

Player gravity: apply manually `y -= g*dt` since CharacterController has no physics.

Enter vehicle: disable CharacterController & player visual; parent to vehicle; VehicleController.enabled true and playerInput driven: while driving, VehicleController reads Input. On exit: place player at door side (car pos + right * -2 with clearance), re-enable.

VehicleController arcade:
- rigidbody: mass 1200, drag .05, angularDrag 1.
- floats: accel 15, maxSpeed 40, brakeForce 30, steerAngle... implement:
  - forwardInput = Input vertical; turn = horizontal.
  - velocity forward speed = transform.InverseTransformDirection(rb.velocity).z
  - if grounded (raycast down), apply force = transform.forward * forwardInput * accel * dt * mass*(1-slope?), clamp speed: if speed > max, no more force.
  - steering: rb.MoveRotation? Add torque: transform.rotation multiply by yaw rate proportional to speed sign and magnitude limited by speed. yawRate = turn * steerCurve(speed) * sign(speed). Use rb.MoveRotation(rb.rotation * Quaternion.Euler(0, yawRate*dt, 0)) — but separate rigidbody + collisions ok.
  - lateral grip: reduce sideways velocity: velocity = forward*speedf + sideways * sidewaysDamp.
  - Sirens for police cars flashing PointLights red/blue alternating. Since max lights… 4 police cars * 2 lights = 8 point lights ok on builtin forward? Might exceed per-object limit but they're separate objects. Keep intensity small. Actually limit: quality settings pixel light count default 4; too many dynamic lights degrade. Make siren lights emissive quads flashing color instead of lights. Simpler & cheap. Yes: two small spheres on top with emissive material color toggling red/blue.

Peds dying: ragdoll = disable collider, rotate 90°, disable nav-ish logic, mark dead, despawn after 10s. Detect vehicle hit: in VehicleController fixed update, do sphere check around front of car for NPCController list (NPCManager static list). speed>4 => kill; wanted +1 star heat.

Police: police officers spawn: count = wanted level; spawn on roads within 60-120m of player, on foot, chase: move toward player: simple transform move w/ CharacterController or just translate on ground with no physics, shoot when within 20m and line of sight: raycast to player, damage over time + muzzle sound. Player killing cop => +1 more star.

WantedSystem heat: kill civ = +20 heat, hit cop = +30, heat thresholds stars = 20.. Use map: stars = min(6, heat/15). Decay: if time since last crime > 10s: heat -= ( policemen? ) 1.5/sec. If stars>0 cops chase.

Camera controller: three modes follow player/car; aim with right mouse rotates yaw/pitch; collision: raycast from pivot to cam, pull in. While driving, camera behind car with yaw following car yaw + mouse offset. Simplify: camera pivot target = player or car; always mouse orbit, plus when in car auto-align yaw gradually to car forward. Fine.

Minimap: separate top-down camera, orthographic, RT 256x256, follows player yaw rotating? GTA minimap rotates with player. Do non-rotating (north-up) with player arrow rotation. Draw dots: for listOfEntities positions relative->screen. Simple.

HUD: OnGUI drawing textures (use Texture2D created at runtime white texture and GUI.Box/Label; stars via ★ characters). Money in yellow. Health bar red. Speed when in car. Minimap: RT camera top-down following player; also draw blips? drawing blips on minimap requires world→map math; doable: positions relative to player scaled. I'll draw simple dots for peds/police/cars on the minimap rect. Nice.

That's a lot of code but let's write it well and compactly. Aim for ~1500-2500 lines total across files. Keep each file focused, well-commented.

Also README with setup:
1. Unity Hub install 2022.3 LTS
2. Open project folder
3. Create empty scene, add WorldBuilder? Better: SceneBuilder editor menu "GTA/Build San Andreas Scene" that creates everything including WorldBuilder objects. Let me include an editor script that creates the scene (EditorSceneManager.NewScene, then builds). The WorldBuilder static BuildAllWorld() used both by editor (instantiating into scene, marked undo-able? not needed) and runtime Start.

NPC flee: when player shoots nearby (NoiseEvent via static Action<Vector3>), NPCs within 25 run away.

Weapon system details:
- input: mouse fire button (also works when aiming), keys 1/2/3 for fist/pistol/SMG.
- weapon def struct: name, damage, fireRate, spread, range, auto, ammo, mag? Keep simple ammoReserve; headshot skip.
- crosshair drawn in HUD center when armed.
- raycast from camera center (like GTA shooting from camera), but only when aiming or always? GTA SA fires toward crosshair always. Fire from player's gun position toward camera ray hit point. Tracer visual from muzzle to hit.

Recoil: camera pitch kick small.

Impact effects: hit NPC -> blood puff particle? Use small particle system created via code (PLAY using Emit). Simplify: puff = spawn sphere shrinking & fading? Use simple particle: create ParticleSystem once and reuse Emit(params). I'll implement a tiny EffectSpawner with (a) blood red particles, (b) dust on car hit, (c) sparks on metal. Particle systems from code with legacy modules - they're standard APIs. Keep small.

Damage to player from cops: also cars hitting player? skip.

Vehicles: several types (sedan, taxi, cop car, sports) with stats and colors; player can jack any car incl. traffic (traffic mark it vehicle then stop its AI). When player enters TrafficAI vehicle: disable AI, full manual control. Exit: resume AI? Keep manual forever (classic jack).

Traffic AI: waypoint grid following, stop at red? no lights - just go; collision avoid: raycast forward: brake if obstacle. At node pick random next direction except reverse. Vehicle list in VehicleManager keeps count: if wrecked explode (fire particles + boom damage nearby + wanted).

Explosions: vehicle health; bullets damage vehicles; at 0 => explode: particles + force + damage nearby actors, wrecked black.

This is getting big but let's do it—comprehensive yet consistent. Total maybe 3000 lines. That's OK but time. Let's aim for efficient but complete (~2000).

Money pickups: coins scattered; killed peds drop cash pickup.

Save logic: GameManager static Instance.

Let me carefully write cohesive, compile-safe C# code. Should be careful about API differences; stick to very standard APIs (UnityEngine.* module, PhysicsModule, UIModule for OnGUI). Unity 2022.3 = C# 9. Standard string interpolation fine (C# 9 supports $"" since C# 6).

File-awareness: namespace GTA. Avoid namespace collision with common words: use `namespace SanAndreasin`? Use `namespace GtaClone`. Ensure class name unique: Weapon? `GtaClone.WeaponData`.

CharacterController component: attach, radius .3, height 1.7, center (0, .9? no: center y = height/2 offset).

Fonts on OnGUI: default.

Also project files: Packages/manifest.json minimal: com.unity.ai.navigation? Not needed (we don't use NavMesh). Keep:
{
  "dependencies": {
    "com.unity.collider-aware-input-system"? no.
Standard minimal: 
{
  "dependencies": {}
}
Unity will add built-in packages automatically (com.unity.ugui? not needed since OnGUI). Actually Unity adds its own default manifest? With empty dependencies it still works — auto-referenced packages remain. To be safe include "com.unity.modules.physics" etc.? Modules auto included via ProjectSettings? Built-in modules are listed in Packages/manifest.json? They're implicit. It works; Unity regenerates missing ones. I'll provide manifest with empty dependencies and note Unity adds defaults.

ProjectSettings: Unity will complain about missing ProjectSettings folder? It creates defaults ("Project Settings were created..."). It works (common practice to open with just Assets & manifest). Add ProjectVersion.txt anyway.

BAD case: This will be a LOT of code. I'll write each file with the write tool. Then a README. Maybe also a copy-paste summary. Also can't test-compile without Unity; note that.

Alternatively, I could check if dotnet/mono is available to at least syntax-check C# files! Let me check `which dotnet csc mcs`. If mono's mcs exists, I can compile with fake UnityEngine stubs... That requires stubbing all APIs — heavy. Not worth it; instead write careful code.

Hmm, but risk of compile errors in ~20 files. To mitigate, keep APIs conservative. Let me recall potential pitfalls:

- rb.velocity vs linearVelocity: in Unity 6 (2023.3+) velocity renamed but velocity still present (deprecated warning). Use `.velocity` with pragma? Deprecated warnings fine. But if user opens with Unity 6, still compiles. OK use velocity, note in README.

- CharacterController.Move returns CollisionFlags. standard.

- ParticleSystem setup via code: ps.playOnAwake... standard.

- OnGUI: standard.

- Rendering: Camera.RenderTexture set: cam.targetTexture = rt. standard.

- Layer setup: LayerMask.NameToLayer and Physics.IgnoreLayerCollision.

- Enum flags fine.

- Time.timeScale.

- Cursor lock: Cursor.lockState = CursorLockMode.Locked in Awake; ESC -> release.

- Input: legacy Input (works in 2022.3 by default; in Unity 6 default is new input system only if package installed — Unity 6 templates still have "Active Input Handling: Input Manager" default? Unity 6 default with URP template uses Input System package? Actually Unity 6 project templates set Active Input Handling to "Both"? The 3D (Built-in) template defaults to old Input Manager. Fine, README note.)

Let me decide namespace: `GtaLike`? I'll use `namespace SanAndreasLike`. Simpler: no namespace at all—fewer issues referencing across files; collisions with Unity types? Our class names: GameManager, HUD, Weapon, Minimap, VehicleController, NPCController, TrafficAI, PoliceOfficer, WantedSystem, WorldBuilder, Sfx, EffectSpawner, PlayerController, CameraController(these exist in Unity? "CameraController" not; "Weapon" no; "GameManager" no; "Minimap" no; "WantedSystem" no). There's UnityEngine.SceneManagement no. Autonomous? ok, no namespace = simplest and cross-references easy
